text:
### Observed differences

- The route mix after A06 changed. Earlier, of A06's observed outgoing transitions, about 53 in 100 led to A07 and about 44 in 100 to A08; in the later window about 41 in 100 lead to A07 and about 53 in 100 to A08, and a transition to A09 appears (about 4 in 100) that was not observed earlier. This rests on roughly 190 outgoing transitions per window and is the most unusual single difference in the evidence, exceeding about 97 in 100 random re-splits. [DIR006]
- Participation shifted between two groups of activities. In the later window, A01, A05, A08 and A09 each appear in about 52–53 in 100 traces (about 45–46 in 100 earlier), while A02, A03, A04, A11 and A12 each appear in about 47–48 in 100 traces (about 55 in 100 earlier); for example, A03 appears in 94 of 200 traces versus 110 of 200 earlier. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC008, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012]
- The repetition-heavy part around A03 is traversed less. A03 and A12 average about 1.0 occurrences per trace in the later window (about 1.2 earlier) and A10 about 0.5 (about 0.7 earlier), while the share of traces in which they repeat stays similar (about 25 in 100 versus 27 in 100 for A03); A07 averages about 0.4 occurrences per trace (about 0.5 earlier) although it appears in a similar share of traces (about 25 in 100). [OCC003, OCC007, OCC010, OCC012]
- Entries into the A03-centred part carry less traffic. From A09, the share of outgoing transitions going to A03 falls from about 48 in 100 to about 41 in 100, while the share returning to A01 rises from about 13 to about 17 in 100; from A02, the share going to A03 falls from about 51 to about 42 in 100. [DIR009, DIR002]
- A07's own exits changed slightly: earlier it returned to A06 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window it does so in about 96 in 100 and occasionally exits to A05 or A09 (about 1–2 in 100 each). [DIR007]
- Two directional profiles rest on too few observations to interpret: A04's outgoing transitions (1 before, 2 after) and A08's (3 before, 8 after) changed markedly in shares but are based on only 1–8 transitions. [DIR004, DIR008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that existing alternative paths are taken with different frequencies, centred on the branch after A06. In the later window, A06 continues to A08 in about 53 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 44 in 100 earlier) rather than to A07 (about 41 in 100, down from about 53 in 100), and A07 now occasionally leaves its loop back to A06 by exiting to A05 or A09; the flow then runs on through A08, A05 and A09, from which a smaller share continues to A03. In line with this, the chain activities A01, A05, A08 and A09 each appear in about 52–53 in 100 traces (about 45–46 in 100 earlier), whereas the cycle around A03 — A03→A12→A10, with A12 also leading to A11→A04 and entered from A02 and A09 — appears in fewer traces (A02, A03, A04, A11 and A12 each about 47–48 in 100 versus about 55 in 100) and is repeated slightly less often (A03/A12 about 1.0 versus about 1.2 occurrences per trace). Supporting signs: the branch shift at A06 is observed directly on about 190 outgoing transitions per window and is the most unusual difference in the set; the participation of nine activities moves exactly in the directions this rerouting predicts, each backed by roughly 90–110 traces per window; and both entries into the A03 cycle, from A02 and from A09, send a smaller share of their traffic to A03 in the later window. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR002, DIR009, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC008, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012]

Limitations: the activities co-occur within the same traces, so the agreeing items are not independent confirmations; no screening baseline is included, so the number of qualifying items cannot be checked against a chance expectation; and the modest reduction in repetitions means the difference is not purely a redistribution between alternatives. The competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is sampling variability between two finite windows of 200 traces — most occurrence differences exceed only about 70–89 in 100 random re-splits, which a stable process produces regularly — so the hypothesis rests chiefly on the direct, unusually large branch shift at A06 together with the coherent direction of the remaining items. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012]

Other differences: In the later window, A05 sends about 6 in 100 of its outgoing transitions directly to A06, which was not observed earlier, and A06 appears in more traces (about 53 in 100 versus about 45 in 100) while its occurrences per trace stay flat, though this last item is well within the chance range (larger than only about 20 in 100 random re-splits). [DIR005, OCC006]
